result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md: waitlist position computed on every read via one new function, getWaitlistPosition(db, eventId, registrationId), added to the existing apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (REQ-020). NO SCHEMA CHANGE NEEDED -- checked apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts directly: registrations.event_id/admission/created_at/id already exist, and registrations_waitlist_order_idx (a partial index on (event_id, created_at) WHERE admission='waitlisted') already exists from REQ-011's schema, built anticipating exactly this query -- so DATA-DESIGNER is not dispatched for this run (same precedent as REQ-017/REQ-020, confirmed explicitly in Sec7 of the design).

QUERY MECHANISM: position = 1 + count of waitlisted rows for the same event that are 'ahead' of the target row, where ahead means created_at strictly earlier, or created_at tied AND id lower (an explicit, stated tie-break for the near-impossible timestamp-collision case, Sec2.3). Expressed as a plain Drizzle eq/lt/and/or filter (no raw SQL, no window function), matching REQ-020 Sec1.2's established 'no raw SQL escape hatch' discipline. The function performs this SELECT count(*) fresh on every call -- no interface anywhere (RegistrationOutcome, RegisterForEventResult, EventRecord, or any new type) gains a position/rank field, so AC3's git grep has nothing to find (Sec2.4).

SCOPING ISSUE RESOLVED EXPLICITLY (Sec0): AC2 references 'withdrawing' a registration, but REQ-022 (withdraw) does not exist yet and depends_on REQ-021, not the reverse. Chose OPTION (B) from the task's named alternatives: the position query is designed to be provably correct by construction (its correctness depends only on the live value of registrations.admission, never on which code path changed it), so AC2 is verified by a direct SQL UPDATE of the admission column in the test fixture rather than by building any withdraw primitive (real or internal-only). Rejected option (a) reasoning: an internal-only withdraw stub risks inventing a subset of REQ-022's real surface (confirm-first gate, seat-freeing, notification-killing, its own audit action) that could diverge from what REQ-022 actually designs later -- this exact 'AC's own stated verification method can't literally run yet' shape already has an accepted precedent in this pipeline, docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md Sec8 open question 3, which named an interim substitute test rather than building a stand-in feature; Sec0 here follows the same move and gives TEST-DESIGNER a precise 5-step runnable substitute case.

Handler wiring (Sec3): handlers/registration.ts's existing waitlisted branch gains one additional read (getWaitlistPosition, called only when outcome.kind==='waitlisted', reusing outcome.registrationId which REQ-020 already returns unconditionally on that branch) and composeRegistrationReply's waitlisted case gains a position line + a new waitlistedWhatNext line; a null position (defensive case) omits the line silently rather than rendering error text (flagged as a judgment call, Sec6 open question 3, not asserted as certain). Two new i18n keys added under the existing Catalog.registration object (waitlistedPositionPrefix, waitlistedWhatNext) following REQ-020's established placeholder-copy convention -- final wording left to CONTENT-BA, with an explicit caution (Sec6 open question 2) that waitlistedWhatNext should not promise a specific auto-promotion timing/mechanism since REQ-023 isn't built yet.

AC4 (unbounded waitlist) needed no new design element -- Sec5 states this as a proof of absence: REQ-020's decideRegistrationOutcome row 8 (the unconditional waitlisted fallback) is unchanged, and getWaitlistPosition is read-only, so nothing in this design could introduce a cap.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md Sec0 resolves the AC2/REQ-022 ordering gap (REQ-022 depends_on REQ-021, so a real withdraw feature cannot exist yet) by naming a direct-SQL test substitute rather than building any withdraw primitive. This is a reasoned choice with a stated precedent (REQ-019 Sec8 open question 3), but CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and TEST-DESIGNER should independently confirm the substitute test in Sec0's closing paragraph actually exercises AC2's claim, rather than taking this design's own say-so as settled.

docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md Sec6 open question 2: the waitlistedWhatNext catalog string risks overpromising a specific auto-promotion mechanism/timing that REQ-023 has not yet built. This design does not draft the literal copy (CONTENT-BA's call) but flags the risk explicitly so the eventual wording doesn't accidentally commit to a guarantee this codebase can't yet keep.
